html:
Volubilis is the ruin of a Berber and Roman town near Meknes, in northern Morocco. It grew from the 3rd century BCE and was one of the main cities of the kingdom of Mauretania, perhaps a capital of King Juba II.

Rome annexed Mauretania in the 40s CE, and Volubilis became the main inland town of the province, rich from olive oil. It has fine mosaics, a basilica and a triumphal arch. Rome pulled back from the area in the late 200s, but people stayed on.

In 788 Idris I, a descendant of the Prophet, arrived there and was accepted as leader by the local Berbers, beginning the Idrisid state. The town was later abandoned for Fez. It became a World Heritage Site in 1997.
